title: Sorting by colour, size and shape
keyIdea: To sort, pick one thing to look at, like colour, size or shape. That is your rule. Things that are the same in that way go together in one group. The same toys can be sorted again with a new rule, and then the groups change. To guess someone's rule, look for what is the same in every group. Say your rule out loud: 'I sorted by colour.'

kid: Look at your toys. Pick one thing to look at. Is it the colour? Put all the red ones here. Put all the blue ones there.
Now try size. Big ones go here. Small ones go there. They are the same toys, but the groups are new.
Try shape. All the circles go in one hoop, all the squares in one, and all the triangles in one. A big red circle and a small blue circle go in the same hoop. They are both circles!
Say how you did it: 'I sorted by shape.' If a toy is in the wrong hoop, move it. To guess a friend's rule, look at each hoop. What is the same?
adult: Sorting is the start of classifying and data handling. Development Matters asks three and four year olds to talk about and compare objects by size and shape, and US Common Core K.MD.B.3 asks children to classify objects into given categories. Each feature, such as colour, size or shape, is an attribute, and the sorting rule (the criterion) says which attribute to use.

The key ideas: sort by one attribute at a time; the same set of objects can be sorted in more than one way; every object must go somewhere by the rule; and you can work out an unknown rule by asking what is the same within each group and different between groups. Explaining the rule out loud is part of the skill, not an extra.

Common mistakes: switching rules halfway, so a small red block ends up with the big ones because the reds are there; grouping by what 'looks nice' with no rule at all; thinking a big circle and a small circle cannot go together; and believing a set can only be sorted one way. A common adult slip is always choosing the rule for the child. Let them pick, then ask them to say it.

In the lab your child drags six toys into hoops by colour, then sorts the same six by size and again by shape, fixes three toys in the wrong hoop, and guesses the rule a friend used from the finished hoops.

familyTip: At tidy-up time, sort together: socks by colour, then the same socks by size. Ask "How did you sort them?" and wait for the rule. Then mix them up and say "Can you sort them a new way?"

visual.caption: Sort by shape. Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: sort the same six toys by colour, by size and by shape, fix the mix-ups, and guess a friend's rule.

practice.prompt: We sort by colour. Where does a red sock go?
choices: With the socks that are big
practice.hint: The rule is colour. What colour is the sock?
practice.explain: The sock is red and the rule is colour, so it goes with the red things.

practice.prompt: There are {a} red blocks and {b} blue blocks. You sort by colour. How many blocks go in the red hoop?
practice.hint: Only the red blocks go in the red hoop.
practice.explain: All {a} red blocks go in the red hoop. The {b} blue blocks go in the blue hoop.

practice.prompt: A big blue circle and a small red circle. We sort by shape. Do they go together?
practice.hint: The rule is shape. Look only at the shape.
practice.explain: Both are circles, so they go in the circle hoop. Colour and size do not matter for this rule.

practice.prompt: The big hoop has {n} toys. You find one more big toy. How many toys are in the big hoop now?
practice.hint: A big toy goes in the big hoop. That is one more.
practice.explain: {n} toys and one more make {=n+1} toys in the big hoop.

pool.prompt: Mia put 🍎 and 🍓 in one hoop, and 🍌 and 🌽 in the other. What was her rule?
pool.hint: What is the same in each hoop?
pool.explain: The apple and the strawberry are red. The banana and the corn are yellow. She sorted by colour.

pool.prompt: We sort by size. Where does a little blue cup go?
pool.hint: The rule is size. Is the cup big or little?
pool.explain: The cup is little and the rule is size, so it goes with the small things.

pool.prompt: You have {a} circles and {b} squares. You sort by shape. How many go in the square hoop?
pool.hint: Only squares go in the square hoop.
pool.explain: The {b} squares go in the square hoop, and the {a} circles go in the circle hoop.

pool.prompt: Can you sort the same toys a new way?
choices: Only if you get new toys
pool.hint: Think of colour, then size, then shape.
pool.explain: The same toys can be sorted by colour, then by size, then by shape. A new rule makes new groups.

pool.prompt: The red hoop has a red ball, a red car and a blue car. Which one is in the wrong hoop?
pool.hint: Check each one: is it red?
pool.explain: The blue car is not red, so it goes in the blue hoop. The red car and the red ball are in the right place.

pool.prompt: There are {n} toys. You sort them into a big hoop and a small hoop. How many toys are in the hoops now?
pool.hint: Every toy goes in one of the hoops.
pool.explain: Each toy goes in one hoop, so all {n} toys are in the hoops.

pool.prompt: Ben sorts by size. He puts a small red block with the big red blocks. What went wrong?
choices: He looked at colour, not size
pool.hint: His rule is size. Is the block big or small?
pool.explain: The rule is size and the block is small, so it goes with the small ones. Ben switched to colour halfway.

pool.prompt: One hoop has only triangles. The other has only circles. What was the rule?
pool.hint: What is the same in each hoop?
pool.explain: Every hoop has one shape, so the rule was shape.
